title: Tanzanian Butter Bean Coconut
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Maharagwe ya Nazi — large butter beans slow-cooked until creamy and simmered in coconut milk with Zanzibar spices. The creamier, more substantial coastal bean dish — butter beans absorb coconut milk even more completely than kidney beans.
longDesc: Butter beans (large white beans) in coconut milk is a Zanzibar coastal favourite — the large beans become almost melting-creamy when properly cooked, and their mild flavour absorbs the coconut-spice sauce completely.
steps: Cook soaked butter beans in fresh water 60—70 minutes until very tender and creamy. Reserve liquid.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add butter beans and ½ cup reserved liquid.
Add coconut milk. Simmer gently 10 minutes.
chefTips: Butter beans must be cooked until extremely tender — almost falling apart.
Their large size means they take longer than kidney beans.
Some will naturally break down into the sauce — this is correct.
commonMistakes: Under-cooking — butter beans should be almost melting.
cookingScience: Butter beans have a lower tannin content than red beans — they become much creamier when cooked because their cell walls break down more readily, releasing starch directly into the sauce. This produces a naturally thicker, more luscious result.
sustainabilityTips: Butter beans are nitrogen-fixing — sustainable protein.
culturalNote: Butter beans in coconut milk are one of Zanzibar's most comforting dishes — the large creamy beans in rich coconut sauce produce a bowl of pure nourishment.
